full_judgment: 27. There is no rule or law which provides that all the charge-sheet witnesses are to be produced before the Court and examined. In a case however where there is no eye-witness or there is hardly any circumstantial evidence, it is essential that the persons who are next-door neighbours or lived near the place of occurrence should be examined for unfolding of the case. Withholding of persons who are considered material under the facts and circumstances of the case casts a serious reflection on the fairness of the trial and an adverse presumption can be drawn.
